strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem—semantic occupancy prediction for legged robots with single panoramic cameras—with clear motivation distinguishing legged from wheeled platforms
Introduces two valuable datasets (QuadOcc: real quadruped data; Human360Occ: comprehensive CARLA-based benchmark) that will enable future research on panoramic perception for embodied AI

Technically sound method integrating well-motivated components: DP-ER exploits complementary geometric properties of raw and equirectangular projections; BGV naturally balances Cartesian (near-field) and cylindrical-polar (far-field ring) reasoning; novel gradient-energy gating in AMoE-3D emphasizes structural boundaries

Strong empirical results surpassing LiDAR baselines on real data (20.56 vs. 18.44 mIoU QuadOcc) and showing substantial cross-domain robustness on H3O (37.29/32.23 within/cross-city, +8.08 on cross-city)

Comprehensive experimental validation including ablations, qualitative comparisons, lighting robustness analysis, and efficiency evaluation demonstrating practical deployment feasibility (14-18 FPS on RTX 4090)
Clear presentation with well-motivated design choices, informative visualizations, and thorough related work positioning
weaknesses: Limited real-world data scope: QuadOcc contains only 10 scenes from single campus domain with one quadruped platform, raising significant generalization concerns to diverse terrains, other legged morphologies (hexapods, bipeds), and varied environments

Ground truth annotation quality lacks validation: semi-automatic pipeline (LiDAR aggregation → Grounded-SAM → 'targeted manual fixes') provides no inter-rater agreement statistics or consistency analysis, potentially introducing systematic biases into performance metrics

Gait Displacement Compensation shows modest gains (+0.39 mIoU), suggesting either jitter is less problematic than motivated or compensation mechanism is insufficient; no direct validation against measured gait patterns or temporal periodicity modeling

Methodological inconsistency: H3O experiments disable raw-projection branch (contradicting core DP-ER design), and loss function excludes relation loss specifically for panoramic data, suggesting configuration tuning is dataset-specific rather than universally applicable

Insufficient ablation analysis: Table 4 doesn't isolate gradient-energy gating vs. attention, hierarchical vs. single-level injection, or cross-grid fusion impact separately, leaving architectural choices incompletely justified

No experiments validating robustness to calibration errors despite acknowledging 'bounded drift' dependency; no online re-calibration mechanism despite practical importance for long-term legged robot deployment
Limited baseline coverage: no quantitative comparison with other panoramic/omnidirectional methods (OmniOcc, OccCylindrical); most adapted methods (MonoScene, VoxFormer) designed for pinhole cameras

Cross-domain concerns: large within/cross-city gap on H3O (37.29→32.23) suggests environment-specific overfitting; no evaluation on alternative quadruped morphologies, gaits, or humanoid platforms; night performance lags baseline (13.50 vs. 14.20 MonoScene)

Reproducibility limitations: code/datasets promised but unavailable at review; missing implementation details (encoder architecture, hyperparameter selection rationale, training time, convergence behavior) limit verification

Incomplete failure analysis: no discussion of failure modes (transparent surfaces, reflective materials, extreme motion), no per-class performance breakdown on challenging scenarios, and computational requirements insufficient to claim 'lightweight' for all platforms
